blocks.title: Volume Conjecture, [9]
blocks.content: Let $J_{N}(K)$ be the $N$-colored Jones polynomial of a knot $K$ evaluated at $\exp(\frac{2\pi\sqrt{-1}}{N})$ . Then $\lim_{Narrow\infty}\frac{\log|J_{N}(I\mathrm{f})|}{N}=\frac{v_{3}}{2\pi}||K||$, where $||K||$ is the Gromov norm (or the simplicial volume) of the complement of $K$ and $v_{3}$ is the hyperbolic volume of the regular ideal tetrahedron. Recent developments toward the Volume Conjecture can be found in [3, 14, 13, 8, 10]. The term $- \frac{\pi^{2}}{6}$ in (3.3) appears so that $V(1,1, \ldots, 1)=0$ since $\mathrm{L}\mathrm{i}_{2}(1)=\frac{\pi^{2}}{6}$ (see for example [6, (1.5)]). (I learned this from [11, \S 5].)

Note that $V$ and $\tilde{V}$ satisfy the same algebraic equations (3.5) but diﬀerent partial diﬀerential equations (3.4) and that the extra terms in (3.6) are necessary to choose an appropriate branch since $\mathrm{L}\mathrm{i}_{2}$ and $\log$ are multivalued func- tions. (I learned this from T. Takata.)

An optimistic limit is not well deﬁned. There are many ambiguities both in choosing $I(N)$ (I did not say anything about the range of the summation in $S(N)$ and the contours in $I(N))$ and in choosing $(\zeta_{1}, \zeta_{2}, \ldots, \zeta_{k})$ .

Following Kashaev [2], the behavior of $S(N)$ for large $N$ may be approximated by $P(N)I(N)$ with suitably chosen contours. Moreover by using the saddle point method (see for example [7, \S 7.2]) we see that $I(N)$ (and $S(N)$ ) behaves like $\exp(\frac{N}{2\pi\sqrt{-1}}\mathrm{o}-\lim\frac{2\pi\sqrt{-1}\log S(N)}{N}Narrow\infty)$ for large $N$ if we choose a solu- tion $(\zeta_{1}, \zeta_{2}, \ldots, \zeta_{k})$ suitably. Even if this is not true I expect that there is a relation between an optimistic limit and the asymptotic behavior of $S(N)$ .
